chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qāsim ibn Sulaymān, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the owned slave, when he falsely accuses a free person, how many lashes he is to be given. He said: “Forty.”
We have already clarified the basis of it in the narration of Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, so there is no point in repeating it.

key_terms.أَرْبَعِينَ: forty lashes, the stated number of the punishment
key_terms.افْتَرَى: falsely accused or fabricated a slanderous allegation
key_terms.الْحُرِّ: the free person, as opposed to a slave
key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكِ: the owned slave or bondservant under legal discussion
key_terms.رِوَايَةِ: the narration or reported hadith cited by the compiler
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ: is to be flogged or lashed as legal punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the hadd punishment for a slave who falsely accuses a free person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the punishment for a slave who commits false accusation against a free person. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that the prescribed punishment is forty lashes, and the compiler notes that the explanation of this ruling was already discussed in an earlier narration.
